sources.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand, 1953 (Harvard-hosted full scan)
sources.locator: §§26H–26J, printed pp. 96–98; §30C, printed pp. 118–119; §§31A–31E and 31G, printed pp. 121–125; §§34A–34D, printed pp. 134–138; §§36A–36D, printed pp. 141–146 (full 198-page scan read in the relevant OCR text)

contents.name: §26H–26I: positive linear functionals, extendability, Schwarz inequality and the positive-definiteness calculus
§26J: Plancherel-type theorem for a semisimple self-adjoint commutative Banach algebra with a positive functional on a dense ideal
§30C: translation continuity of L^1 functions and its use in the classification of characters
§31A–31C: convolution in L^1(G), commutativity, associativity and the norm inequality
§31D: the unit criterion — L^1(G) has an identity exactly when G is discrete
§31E: approximate identities in L^1(G) and the convergence u_U*f -> f
§31G: positive linear functionals on L^1(G) are continuous
§34A: alpha_M(x)=f_x(M)/f(M) is a character independent of f, uniformly continuous and jointly continuous in (x,M); u_x(M)->alpha_M(x) along approximate identities
§34B: M -> alpha_M is a bijection onto all characters; the transform formula f(M)=int f(x)alpha_M(x) dx
§34C: the topology of the dual is the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets
§34D: pointwise products of characters and local compactness of the dual
§36A: positive definite functions on G as Fourier-Stieltjes transforms of finite positive measures; uniform continuity corollary
§36B: inversion theorem on the L^1∩P core; construction of the dual measure m and proof that m is the Haar measure
§36C: the inversion formula determines a unique Haar measure on the dual once the measure on G is fixed; explicit normalisations
§36D: the Plancherel theorem, T* = T^{-1} on L^2, and the abstract Plancherel theorem of §26J
§§25 and 26 general commutative Banach algebra theory (maximal ideals, characters, spectra) used through the earlier Gelfand page

sources.title: T. W. Koerner, Topological Groups (author lecture notes, Internet Archive snapshot of the author PDF; the dpmms.cam.ac.uk host currently serves an incomplete TLS chain to Node/curl)

contents.name: §10 Definition 10.1 (finite regular measures M(X)) and Exercise 10.2 (regular measures are carried by sigma-compact open subgroups)
§10 Lemma 10.3: convolution of finite regular measures is finite regular; Exercise 10.4: M(G) is a commutative Banach algebra with unit
§10 Exercise 10.5 and Theorem 10.6: uniqueness theorem — a finite measure on the dual with vanishing inverse transform is zero
§11 Example 11.1: inversion fails for arbitrary L^1 functions without an integrability hypothesis; the transform of a compactly supported continuous function need not be integrable
contents.reason: This is the Euclidean failure example motivating the hypotheses of the inversion theorem; the companion functional-analysis page already owns the R^n inversion and its counterexamples, so no item is minted here.

contents.name: §11 Theorem A: inversion on the class of transforms of finite measures
§11 Lemma 11.2 and Definition 11.3: transforms of positive measures are continuous positive definite; finite-matrix definition of positive definiteness
§11 Theorem B = Theorem 12.3 (Bochner): continuous positive definite functions are exactly the transforms of finite positive measures
§11 Lemma 11.4: f*g of L^2 functions is continuous and f*f~ is positive definite
§12 Lemma 12.1: elementary positivity identities, |phi(x)|<=phi(0), uniform continuity of continuous positive definite functions
§12 Lemma 12.2: the double integral of f(x)f*(y)phi(x-y) is nonnegative for f in L^1(G)
§12 Theorem 12.4: existence of a dual Haar measure making inversion hold (the normalisation convention)
§12 Exercise 12.5: consistency of the new Haar convention with the compact and discrete conventions
§12 Theorem 12.6 (Plancherel on L^1 ∩ L^2) and Theorem 12.7 (linear isometry L^2(G) -> L^2(dual))
§12 Lemma 12.8: every L^2 function on the dual is a product of transforms — the range-density input
contents.reason: The surjectivity and range-density statements are proved on FR-17 from Pontryagin biduality; FR-16 deliberately states only the isometric extension, so this lemma is spent there and is not scaffolded here.

contents.name: Appendix C.2 Theorem C.4 (Haar): existence, uniqueness up to scale, positivity on open sets and finiteness on compact sets
Appendix C.3 Theorem C.6: the character group of an LCA group is LCA; a separating subgroup is dense
Appendix C.3 basic properties of the Fourier transform: separating self-adjoint algebra dense in C_0(dual); convolution to product; ||f^||_inf <= ||f||_1
Appendix C.3 Lemma C.7: discrete dual of a compact group and compact dual of a discrete group
Appendix C.3 Theorem C.8 (Parseval formula) for L^2 functions
Appendix C.3 inverse Fourier transform of a measure and the positive-definite condition (C.1); Theorem C.9 (Herglotz–Bochner)
Appendix C.3 Theorem C.10 (Inversion Theorem): normalisation of the dual Haar measure, Fourier expansion on T and the compact-group orthonormal-basis remark
Appendix C.3 Theorem C.11: for compact abelian G the characters separate points and form a complete orthonormal basis of L^2(G)
contents.reason: Point separation and the compact-group orthonormal basis use Pontryagin duality; FR-17 owns the separation lemma so that FR-16 stays free of biduality.

contents.name: Appendix C.3 Theorem C.12 (Pontryagin duality) and Theorem C.13 (subgroups, quotients, annihilators)
contents.reason: Biduality and annihilator exactness are exactly the FR-17 pair's commissioned content; using them here would recreate the circular route the design forbids.

contents.name: Appendix C.3 Example C.14(1)-(2): the duals of Z and R
Appendix C.3 Example C.14(3)-(5): duals of locally compact fields, Q_p, and the solenoid dual of Q
contents.reason: Owner scope decision (2026-10-05): out of scope with no destination. FR-15 A/B currently covers only the elementary duals of Z, T, Euclidean space, and finite cyclic groups. No planned item or interface consumes the Q_p, locally compact field, or solenoid computations; adding them would materially expand FR-15.

contents.name: Appendix C.3 Lemma C.15 (Riemann–Lebesgue for absolutely continuous measures) and Lemma C.16
contents.reason: Lemma C.15 is the measure-density form of the Euclidean Riemann–Lebesgue statement and Lemma C.16 a measure-theoretic restatement on S^1; the LCA vanishing-at-infinity theorem is proved here directly from the compact unitisation spectrum instead.
